title: The Airline Bumped Me. I Knew The Federal Rule.
script: My flight was overbooked, and the gate agent picked me to get bumped for checking in last. She offered a $200 voucher and a seat the next morning. I said no thanks, and asked for the compensation the airline has to pay by federal law when your flight leaves without you. She insisted the voucher was the only option. I pulled up the exact rule on my phone and read her the payout for a domestic delay under two hours: four times my fare, paid on the spot, cash or check, never a coupon. Her supervisor showed up already annoyed, ready to repeat the same voucher script. I read him the regulation number instead. He vanished for ten minutes and came back with a check for $1,700 and an apology that sounded rehearsed. Then he mentioned the next flight still had free upgrades. I took the aisle seat in first class, ordered the steak, and toasted the gate agent who tried to hand me a coupon instead of the law.
